text:
The Nifty 500 closed at 23,734.2, down 0.55% on the day, while Bank Nifty slipped to 61,034.1, a 0.79% decline. Both indices fell despite a healthy breadth score of 75.7, with 157 advances against 332 declines, indicating the move was fairly broad‑based. The 20‑day, 50‑day and 200‑day moving averages still sit above half the stocks (81.8%, 59.2% and 50.6% respectively), showing the market remains in a generally bullish zone but under pressure.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding INR 5,736.55 crore today, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 2,253.58 crore, extending a 12‑day buying streak for FIIs and a 10‑day selling streak for DIIs. The sector map shows “Leading” groups such as PSU banks, capital markets and auto were strong, whereas “Weakening” areas include IT, pharma and infrastructure. In the options market, Nifty’s put‑call ratio (PCR) is 0.83, with a max‑pain level at 25,100 and a call wall at 26,000, suggesting modest bullish bias. Bank Nifty’s PCR is 1.24, max‑pain at 59,000 and a call wall at 61,000, indicating some resistance near the current 61,038 level.

Watch the Nifty pivot points around 25,148 (pivot) and 25,242 (R1) and Bank Nifty’s pivot at 61,038 with resistance at 61,296. Key headlines to monitor include the “Sensex, Nifty edge down on profit taking, inflation worries” and the “FIIs and India are back together” flow note, which could influence next‑session sentiment. Also keep an eye on US Treasury and Fed rate commentary, as any shift may affect the INR‑USD rate (currently 94.23) and broader risk appetite.
